description: Q1 privileged access review for the configuration management and fraud tooling platforms was completed three weeks late and did not include documented challenge of all exceptions; several legacy admin accounts remain.

Discovery of a legacy admin group with broad, non-role-based privileges in a core AuroraPay configuration service (related to INC5); group membership and associated service accounts have not yet been fully remediated.

Multiple latency incidents impacting AuroraPay Debit authorizations over a six-week period share similar symptoms, but post-incident reviews have not converged on a single root cause or structural remediation plan.

Several auxiliary services and vendor integrations are not yet fully onboarded into centralized security logging; current coverage limits the ability to correlate events across the full AuroraPay stack.

Following the January–February social engineering scam spike (INC3), fraud rules and velocity checks have not yet been fully tuned to address observed patterns in high-risk accounts and receiving destinations.

Customer education on scams is available on the public website and in periodic campaigns, but is not consistently surfaced in high-risk flows such as first-time high-value e-Transfer sends on mobile channels.

Post-incident review of the January fraud analytics vendor outage (INC7) identified that contracted RTO/RPO and actual performance were misaligned; updated contractual commitments and technical resiliency measures are still under negotiation.

Documentation of the February e-Transfer outage (INC1) for regulatory reporting lacked clear linkage to risk appetite, residual risk assessment, and effectiveness of completed remediation, limiting ability to demonstrate control over operational resilience.
